notes.text:
The collection has a generic BM `rei-miro-britanico` record, but its supporting source gives no distinguishing description or accession. Several BM rei miro records in this batch could fit it. The catalogue labels this combined field “Found/Acquired”; it is retained as source wording and is not treated as an independently established findspot. A separate “Production place” field is represented as made_at when present.

30 September 2026 identity review: ambiguous crosswalk to `rei-miro-britanico`; keep this catalogue source unlinked. The British Museum identifies Museum number Oc.7834, CDMS Oc1872C1.7834 and miscellaneous number Oc1872C0514.25 (https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/E_Oc-7834). It describes a wooden crescent breast-plate/neck ornament with male heads and chin tufts at both ends, 20 × 48.3 × 3.5 cm, produced on Easter Island before 1872. The accession note records W.D. Cutter's sale to A.W. Franks from Frederick Dally's collection on 10 May 1872 and presentation to the BM on 14 May 1872. These details establish this catalogue identity and distinguish it from Oc.6330 and Oc,+.2601. The Arte row for `rei-miro-britanico` gives only type and holder, so it cannot identify Oc.7834. Resolution needs a primary description or image tied to that row, or a historical crosswalk to this accession.
